intro: Mark what Dessalines says must happen (Claim) and why he says it (Reason). Then tap Check.
before_we_talk: BEFORE WE TALK: These were real people, and what happened to them shaped the world we live in. Use their names and their words. No jokes, and no comparisons to everyday life.
citation: Jean-Jacques Dessalines, Haitian Declaration of Independence, January 1, 1804 (excerpt), from New Visions lesson G2.02.D.2
text: “It is not enough to have expelled the barbarians who have bloodied our land for two centuries; … We must, with one last act of national authority, forever assure the empire of liberty in the country of our birth; we must take any hope of re-enslaving us away from the inhuman government …. In the end we must live independent or die.”

key.phrase: we must live independent or die
key.why: What he says must happen: independence, or death.

key.phrase: forever assure the empire of liberty in the country of our birth
key.why: The same goal, said another way: liberty, for good.

key.phrase: the barbarians who have bloodied our land for two centuries
key.why: What was done to them: they “bloodied our land.”
The danger he names: that slavery could come back.
